description: config:recommended already covers every ecosystem Renovate can detect on its own: npm/pnpm (the root manifest, the four workspace manifests, pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides), pep621 (14 pyproject.toml files plus uv.lock), cargo (packages/core/ticks), github-actions (every `uses:` in .github/workflows) and the Docker images in Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml.

What it could NOT see, and what the customManagers below now cover, are the desktop bootstrap's own toolchain pins: the Node runtime, pnpm release and uv build recorded in packages/apps/desktop/resources/bootstrap/tool-manifest.json and in the generator that produces it. Those are hash-and-signature pinned, so a Renovate PR against them is a work order, not a merge candidate - see the bootstrap rule's prBodyNotes.

Deliberately NOT managed: requirements.lock, supply-chain/audit-tooling.lock and brokers.lock. requirements.lock is a hashed EXPORT of uv.lock (scripts/check-uv-lock-export-drift.py fails when the two disagree) and brokers.lock is derived from it (scripts/check-brokers-lock.py), so they must be regenerated from their source, never bumped in place. Renovate's pip_requirements manager does not match a .lock suffix, so no explicit ignore is needed - this note exists so nobody adds one.

customManagers.description: Bootstrap toolchain: the Node runtime the Electron shell downloads on first run. Pinned in tool-manifest.json and in the generator's own constant, so both move in one PR.

Bootstrap toolchain: the pnpm release the Electron shell enables via corepack. Must stay identical to the root packageManager field, which the npm manager updates - scripts/check-toolchain-freshness.py fails when the two drift.
Bootstrap toolchain: the uv build that provisions the managed Python. Pinned in tool-manifest.json and in the generator's own constant.

packageRules.description: Broker SDKs move real money. Never automerged, always founder-reviewed, and a bump also needs brokers.lock regenerated (the sha256 and licence evidence are pinned per version).
prBodyNotes: **brokers.lock is not updated by this PR.** After reviewing, regenerate the pinned evidence and re-run the gates:

packageRules.description: JavaScript never automerges: the terminal is the order-entry surface and pnpm-lock.yaml changes have to be read.

engines.node is NOT Renovate's to raise. flint.toml [requirements].node_requires is the single source of truth for the floor and tests/test_minimum_requirements_single_source.py pins five package.json files to it. The floor is set by what the dependency tree genuinely needs (jsdom 30's >=22.22.2 today), so a Renovate bump here breaks installs on platforms that are fine. Move flint.toml first; scripts/check-toolchain-freshness.py is what notices when the floor reaches end of life.

Bootstrap toolchain pins are hash- and signature-verified, so the version string is only half the change. A Renovate PR here is a work order: it will fail `pnpm --filter @flinttrade/desktop verify:bootstrap-manifest` until the checksums, the detached signature and the mirrored release key are refreshed and the manifest is REGENERATED. Never hand-edit a digest.
prBodyNotes: **This PR bumps a version string only. The manifest must be regenerated before it can merge.**

`verify:bootstrap-manifest` (supply-chain.yml) fails closed until the checked-in checksum sources match the new version, and `key-freshness.yml` fails if the mirrored Node release key is not currently valid for it. Node releases are signed by whichever release manager cut them, so a Node bump can also require a NEW mirrored key.
#    (SHASUMS256.txt, SHASUMS256.txt.sig and the signer's .asc for Node; sha256.sum for uv)

packageRules.description: The bootstrap Node pin may drift forward inside its release line automatically, but a LINE move (22 -> 24) is a deliberate decision: it has to agree with flint.toml [requirements].node_target and it usually arrives with a different release manager's signing key. scripts/check-toolchain-freshness.py is what raises the line move.
pnpm and the root packageManager field are the same pin in two files; group them so they can never merge apart.
Action digests are pinned to a SHA with a version comment. Renovate maintains both; keep it non-automerged so a supply-chain change to a third-party action is always read by a human.
